title: A fountain for sin; the end of false prophecy; "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered" (Zech 13)
speaker: The LORD of Armies (through the prophet)
description: A fountain is opened for David's house and Jerusalem for sin and impurity; idols and prophets are removed, and a would-be prophet will deny his calling; the sword is called against "my shepherd, the man who is my companion": strike the shepherd and the sheep scatter; two-thirds perish, a third is refined and says "The LORD is my God".

interpretations.label: Fulfilled in Jesus's arrest and the scattering of the disciples
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Jesus applies 13:7 to his arrest and the disciples' flight; "the man who is my companion" implies one equal with the LORD (Guzik); Keil sees the turning of God's hand to the little ones realised first in the apostles. Objection: Mitchell holds that the shepherd is the object of the LORD's indignation (continuing ch. 11) and that Jesus's use is illustrative, not a strict fulfilment.

interpretations.label: The worthless shepherd of ch. 11, punished
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: 13:7–9 continues 11:4–17 (same author, soon after Raphia); "my shepherd" and "my companion" designate the ruler against whom the LORD's sword is called.
